class.name: Landscape3D
class.brief_description: A large, sculptable, texture-splatted heightmap terrain, in the spirit of CryEngine's terrain system.
class.description: [Landscape3D] renders a [TerrainData] heightmap ([member terrain_data]) through a GPU-driven quadtree. The whole terrain is drawn from one small grid mesh, a patch of 16×16 quads, instanced once for every quadtree node on screen: each level up the tree covers twice the ground at half the density, from level 0, which draws every heightmap sample, up to a single root node covering the whole terrain. Every frame a compute shader walks the tree and chooses the nodes to draw by their screen-space error ([member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/level_of_detail/pixel_error]): how far each node's surface strays from the full resolution heightmap, projected to pixels at its distance from the camera. Flat ground stays coarse however close it is, while rugged ground keeps its detail far away. The chosen patches are culled against the camera's view and written straight into indirect draw commands, so how many of them are drawn is never even known to the CPU. Where neighboring patches are drawn at different levels, the finer one's edge is fitted onto the coarser one's vertices, which keeps the surface watertight without skirts. Lighting uses per-pixel normals taken from the full resolution heightmap, so a distant, coarsely drawn patch is shaded exactly like a close one. The Compatibility renderer, which has no compute shaders, makes the same selection on the CPU (see [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/level_of_detail/gpu_lod_enabled]). Near the camera, micro detail refines the ground past the heightmap's own resolution ([member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/micro_detail/levels]): the heightmap is interpolated smoothly there, and every [TerrainLayer] with a [member TerrainLayer.displacement] raises and sinks the ground along its [member TerrainLayer.height_texture], so that pebbles, cobbles and cracks stand out of the ground in silhouette and cast shadows rather than only showing in its shading. Up to 16 [TerrainLayer]s ([member layers]) can be painted onto the terrain, or fewer, as [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/material_layers/max_layers] sets. Every point on the terrain has its own independent weight for every layer (see [TerrainData]'s description); what's actually rendered there is every layer's material mixed in proportion to its share of the total weight, the same "weight-blended" model CryEngine and UE4/5's Landscape layers use, so any number of layers can overlap smoothly at once (not just two at a time) and painting one layer smoothly displaces the others rather than producing hard edges at the vertex grid. A [member Landscape3D.collision_layer] configurable grid of [HeightMapShape3D] tiles, 256 quads a side, is kept in sync automatically so physics bodies collide with the terrain, and an edit only rebuilds the tiles it touches; see [method update_collision]. While selected in the editor, a toolbar appears in the 3D viewport with two lists of brushes, laid out after Unreal Engine's landscape tools: one for sculpting (raising, lowering, smoothing, and flattening the heightmap, and cutting or filling holes - openings in the terrain's geometry itself, e.g. for a cave entrance, that the camera and physics bodies can pass through, see [method TerrainData.is_hole]), and one for painting, erasing and blending the material layers chosen in its [b]MatLayers[/b] list, optionally only on ground within a range of heights and slopes. Holding [kbd]Shift[/kbd] turns Raise into Lower, Paint into Erase and Hole into Unhole (and back), and the mouse wheel over the terrain sizes the brush. The same operations are available from a script through [method sculpt], [method paint_layer], and [method set_hole], for example to carve a crater into the terrain at runtime. The inspector's [b]Import Heightmap...[/b] button imports a square grayscale image as the whole heightmap (see [method TerrainData.import_heightmap] for format/precision recommendations - EXR or HDR, not PNG or a lossy format), creating a [TerrainData] automatically if [member terrain_data] isn't set yet; this replaces the current heightmap and is not undoable. Next to it, [b]Import Layer Mask...[/b] and [b]Generate Layer Mask...[/b] fill in a layer's weights from an image or from the terrain's own shape (see [method TerrainData.import_layer_mask] and [method TerrainData.generate_layer_mask]). How every landscape in a project is drawn - its level of detail, micro detail, virtual texturing, occlusion culling and parallax occlusion mapping - and how many material layers it may use are project settings, under [b]Landscape3D[/b] in the Project Settings (see [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/level_of_detail/pixel_error] and the settings next to it). Every [Landscape3D] follows them as soon as they change. [FoliagePainter3D] and [FoliageSpawner3D] both recognize a [Landscape3D] as a paintable/projectable ground surface alongside [MeshInstance3D], so vegetation can be scattered directly onto it. Roads, rivers and streams are laid over the terrain along splines with [LandscapeSpline3D], and lakes within closed ones; it also shapes the ground under them and paints a layer there. The terrain also acts as an occluder ([member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/occlusion_culling/enabled]): once occlusion culling is enabled (see [member ProjectSettings.rendering/occlusion_culling/use_occlusion_culling], or [member Viewport.use_occlusion_culling] for a custom viewport), whatever stands behind a hill or a ridge is skipped entirely instead of being drawn and then hidden by the terrain. This is what keeps a densely vegetated terrain affordable, since the [FoliagePainter3D]/[FoliageSpawner3D] cells behind a slope are usually most of the vegetation in view. No baking or extra nodes are involved: each block of 32×32 quads hands the renderer a simplified copy of its own surface, kept up to date as the terrain is sculpted. [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/parallax_occlusion_mapping/enabled] is a master switch for Parallax Occlusion Mapping: it must be [code]true[/code] here [i]and[/i] on each individual [TerrainLayer] ([member TerrainLayer.pom_enabled]) for that layer to use it, so a layer with no real height detail never pays for the ray-marching this adds. An enabled layer's [member TerrainLayer.height_texture] gives it extra apparent surface depth (bumps, grooves) from the shader offsetting its texture lookups, without adding any actual geometry. [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/parallax_occlusion_mapping/self_shadow_enabled] additionally darkens crevices that would be shadowed by nearby raised detail, approximated using the fixed [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/parallax_occlusion_mapping/shadow_light_direction] rather than any actual light in the scene (a plain shader can't see scene lights the way a light-processor function can). Independently, [member TerrainLayer.triplanar_enabled] projects a layer's textures from world-space planes instead of a single UV, useful for steep terrain (cliffs) where ordinary UVs would stretch. [b]Note:[/b] Everything is laid out in this node's own space: layer textures stay attached to the ground when the node is moved or rotated. Level of detail is measured there too, so a non-uniform scale skews it.

method.name: get_aabb
method.description: Returns a local-space bounding box around the whole terrain: its footprint, from its lowest to its highest sample, widened by the most micro detail can raise or sink it.

method.name: get_height_region
method.description: Returns [member terrain_data]'s heights covering [param region]; see [method TerrainData.get_height_region].

method.name: get_height_regions
method.description: Returns [member terrain_data]'s heights for each of [param regions], one array per region in the same order; the batched form of [method get_height_region].

method.name: get_hole_region
method.description: Returns [member terrain_data]'s hole flags covering [param region]; see [method TerrainData.get_hole_region].

method.name: get_layer_weight_region
method.description: Returns [member terrain_data]'s weights for the [TerrainLayer] at [param layer_index] covering [param region]; see [method TerrainData.get_layer_weight_region].

method.name: get_layer_weight_regions
method.description: Returns [member terrain_data]'s weights for the [TerrainLayer] at [param layer_index] for each of [param regions], one array per region in the same order; the batched form of [method get_layer_weight_region].

method.name: get_virtual_texture
method.description: Returns the runtime virtual texture the terrain is shaded from (see [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/virtual_texture/enabled]), or an empty [RID] while it doesn't use one. It can be sampled by other materials too, with the UV that [method get_virtual_texture_volume] maps to.

method.name: get_virtual_texture_size
method.description: Returns the size of the runtime virtual texture the terrain is shaded from, in texels a side, or [code]0[/code] while it doesn't use one. See [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/virtual_texture/texel_size].

method.name: get_virtual_texture_volume
method.description: Returns the part of the world the runtime virtual texture is drawn from, as given to [method RenderingServer.texture_virtual_set_runtime_volume]: a unit cube whose X and Z axes run along the texture's U and V, over the whole terrain, and whose Y axis spans its height.

method.name: paint_layer
method.description: Paints the [TerrainLayer] at [param layer_index] in [member layers] within [param radius] meters of [param local_position] (in this node's local space; only the X and Z coordinates matter), by [param strength] per call (a value around [code]0.1[/code] to [code]1.0[/code] is typical), tapering towards the edge of the brush as [param falloff] says (see [method sculpt]). What painting does is up to [param operation]: - [constant PAINT_ADD] raises the layer's weight. Every other layer's weight at each affected point is lowered proportionally so the total stays roughly constant (see [TerrainData]'s description), so repeatedly painting one layer converges on it fully replacing whatever was there rather than just capping out at an even split with it. - [constant PAINT_ERASE] lowers the layer's weight, handing what it loses to the other layers in proportion to their share, which brings back whatever it was painted over. Where no other layer has any weight left, it goes back to the first layer, the ground a new terrain starts out as; erasing the first layer itself there would leave bare ground, so its weight stays. - [constant PAINT_BLEND] averages every layer's weight with its neighbors', softening the edges between layers; [param layer_index] still has to be a layer in use, but does not matter otherwise. Painting can be kept to part of the ground: only where its height (in this node's local space) is within [param height_range] ([code]x[/code] to [code]y[/code]) and its slope within [param slope_range] ([code]x[/code] to [code]y[/code] degrees, [code]0[/code] being flat ground and [code]90[/code] a vertical wall), fading out over [param height_falloff] meters and [param slope_falloff] degrees beyond each end, as with [method TerrainData.generate_layer_mask]. The defaults paint everywhere. Only the layers in use can be painted (see [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/material_layers/max_layers]). Re-uploads only the painted region of the weight maps it changed; painting never changes geometry, so nothing else is rebuilt.

method.name: paint_layer_regions
method.description: Raises the weight of the [TerrainLayer] at [param layer_index] to at least the matching value (from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]) in [param weights] at every sample of each of [param regions], taking what it gains out of the other layers the same way [method paint_layer] does. Samples where the layer already weighs as much are left alone, so painting the same weights twice changes nothing the second time. [LandscapeSpline3D] paints under a road or river with this.

method.name: sculpt
method.description: Sculpts [member terrain_data]'s heightmap within [param radius] meters of [param local_position] (in this node's local space; only the X and Z coordinates matter). [param falloff] shapes the stamp from its center to its rim: [code]1[/code] (the default) tapers across the whole radius, [code]0[/code] applies at full strength right up to the rim and stops dead, leaving a hard edge, and values between hold an inner core at full strength and fade only the outside of it. [param strength] is the maximum height change, in meters, applied at the center of the brush per call, with two exceptions. For [constant SCULPT_FLATTEN] it is how far each height moves towards [param flatten_height] (as a 0-1 fraction; values at or above 1 snap immediately). For [constant SCULPT_SMOOTH] it is the number of averaging passes to smooth by, because smoothing has no per-stamp amount to scale: averaging a vertex with its neighbors is one pass however hard it is applied, so beyond a full blend to that average there is nothing more for strength to do. [code]1[/code] takes the edge off, and higher values flatten out progressively larger bumps (below [code]1[/code], it is one pass applied partially). Refreshes the quadtree nodes and GPU textures under the brush and, unless [param update_collision] is [code]false[/code], also updates the collision tiles under the brush immediately; pass [code]false[/code] while repeatedly sculpting in a tight loop (e.g. dragging a brush) and call [method update_collision] once afterwards instead, since rebuilding a collision tile on every call is comparatively expensive.

method.name: set_height_region
method.description: Writes [param heights] into [member terrain_data] at [param region] (see [method TerrainData.set_height_region]) and refreshes the part of the terrain it covers. See [method sculpt] for [param update_collision].

method.name: set_height_regions
method.description: Writes one array of heights into each of [param regions], in the same order; the batched form of [method set_height_region]. The occluders along the regions are rebuilt once however many of them they border, and each collision tile under them (when [param update_collision] is [code]true[/code]) once for the whole edit, which makes this much cheaper than one [method set_height_region] call per region for edits scattered across many small regions, such as a road along its whole length. Emits [signal terrain_changed] for each region.

method.name: set_hole
method.description: Sets or clears the hole flag within [param radius] meters of [param local_position] (in this node's local space; only the X and Z coordinates matter) and refreshes the part of the terrain it covers. [b]Note:[/b] holes only affect the rendered geometry, not the collision shape (see the class description and [method TerrainData.is_hole]); [param update_collision] is accepted for consistency with [method sculpt] and [method set_height_region] but has no effect here.

method.name: set_hole_region
method.description: Writes [param holes] into [member terrain_data] at [param region] (see [method TerrainData.set_hole_region]) and refreshes the part of the terrain it covers (holes remove geometry; see [method TerrainData.is_hole]).

method.name: set_layer_weight_region
method.description: Writes [param weights] for the [TerrainLayer] at [param layer_index] into [member terrain_data] at [param region] (see [method TerrainData.set_layer_weight_region]) and re-uploads that region of the layer's weight map. Unlike [method paint_layer], this does not touch any other layer's weight, so it won't by itself keep the total weight at each point normalized (see [TerrainData]'s description) - prefer [method paint_layer] for brush-style painting.

method.name: set_layer_weight_regions
method.description: Writes one array of weights for the [TerrainLayer] at [param layer_index] into each of [param regions], in the same order, without touching any other layer; the batched form of [method set_layer_weight_region].

method.name: update_collision
method.description: Brings the terrain's collision up to date with the current [member terrain_data] heights, rebuilding only the [HeightMapShape3D] tiles whose heights changed. Called automatically when [member terrain_data] changes and after each editor brush stroke; call it manually after scripted edits made with their [code]update_collision[/code] argument set to [code]false[/code].

members.member: The terrain's shadow casting mode, as [member GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow]. The terrain is drawn into shadow maps from a list of patches of its own, which also holds those outside the camera's view, since they can still cast shadows into it (see [member shadow_distance]); it is the same selection the camera sees, so the two never disagree about where the ground is. [constant GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_DOUBLE_SIDED] behaves like [constant GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_ON].
The terrain's physics collision layer, equivalent to [member CollisionObject3D.collision_layer].
The terrain's physics collision mask, equivalent to [member CollisionObject3D.collision_mask].
Shows how the terrain is tessellated; see [enum DebugView].

The terrain's global illumination mode, as [member GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode]. Defaults to [constant GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_STATIC], unlike most small scattered geometry, since a terrain is usually a good candidate for baked lighting.

The ground materials this terrain can be painted with, in the order the editor's [b]MatLayers[/b] list shows them. See [TerrainLayer] and the class description. Only the first [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/material_layers/max_layers] of them (at most 16) are drawn and can be painted; any more are kept, but left out, with a warning.

Patches farther than this from the camera, in meters, cast no shadows; [code]0[/code] means no limit. The terrain is drawn into every shadow map (every split of a [DirectionalLight3D]'s, every other shadowed light's) from its own list of patches, so limiting it can save a lot of vertex work. Keep it at least as large as the largest [member DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_max_distance] in use, plus the length of the longest shadows the terrain should cast into it.

The [TerrainData] this node renders, sculpts, and collides with. A new, empty (flat) [TerrainData] is often the fastest way to start; assign one and use the editor brush to sculpt it, or [method TerrainData.import_heightmap] to start from an existing heightmap image.

The layers of the terrain's runtime virtual texture: geometry whose [member GeometryInstance3D.virtual_texture_draw_layers] shares a bit with these is drawn into it, over the ground. The terrain draws itself into it through these too, so at least one is always set.

signal.name: terrain_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the terrain's surface changes: after heights are edited within [param region] (in [member terrain_data]'s samples, as with [method set_height_region]), whether by [method sculpt], the region setters or [method LandscapeSpline3D.apply_to_landscape]; and for the whole terrain when a different [member terrain_data] is assigned, the assigned one is edited directly, or this node moves. Whatever sits on the surface can refresh just the part of itself standing on [param region]; [LandscapeSpline3D] does.

constants.constant: Raises the height within the brush.
Lowers the height within the brush.
Averages the height within the brush with its immediate neighbors, smoothing out sharp detail.
Moves the height within the brush towards a fixed target height (see [method sculpt]'s [code]flatten_height[/code] parameter), flattening it.
Raises the layer's weight within the brush, taking it from the other layers.
Lowers the layer's weight within the brush, handing it to the other layers (or, where none has any weight left, to the first layer).
Averages every layer's weight within the brush with its neighbors', softening the edges between layers.
Tints every patch with the color of its quadtree level.
Draws the edges of every triangle over the terrain, colored by quadtree level, with patch borders drawn thicker.

Tints green the ground shaded from the runtime virtual texture (see [member ProjectSettings.landscape_3d/virtual_texture/enabled]), the more so the more it is; untinted ground blends its layers in every pixel.
